clinical_notes: 55 y/o with chronic low back pain x 4 months. Completed 8 weeks of supervised PT and trial of NSAIDs without meaningful relief. Exam: positive straight-leg raise on the right at 40 degrees, intact strength and reflexes. Provider requesting lumbar MRI to evaluate for disc herniation. Prior lumbar MRI 9 months ago showed mild multilevel degenerative changes without focal herniation. No interval surgery. No new neurological deficit since prior imaging.
ground_truth_reasoning: C.1 met: 8 weeks documented PT + NSAIDs.
L.1 triggered: prior MRI 9 months ago (within 12-month window).
L.1 exception NOT met: no new deficit, no significant change, no post-op, no radiation.
Frequency limit excludes coverage → DENIED.
policy_excerpt:
CMS LCD L34522 §C.1: Lumbar MRI is covered after documented failure of >=6 weeks conservative therapy.
§L.1 (FREQUENCY LIMIT): Repeat lumbar MRI within 12 months of a prior study is NOT covered unless one of the following is documented: (a) new neurologic deficit since prior imaging, (b) significant clinical change, (c) post-operative evaluation, or (d) interval radiation therapy. Routine surveillance imaging for chronic pain is excluded.

clinical_notes: 59 y/o with right L5 radiculopathy. Completed 4 weeks of formal billed PT plus an additional 4 weeks of supervised home exercise program directed by the PT (total 8 weeks). Initial submission included only the 4 weeks of formal billed PT and was denied for insufficient conservative therapy duration. Provider appealed, submitting the home exercise documentation and a letter from the PT verifying the supervision and progression. EMG confirms L5 radiculopathy.
ground_truth_reasoning: Initial denial: 4 weeks formal PT < 6-week C.1 requirement.
Appeal submission: 4 additional weeks of supervised home exercise documented by PT with progression notes.
§A.7 explicitly allows home exercise to count toward duration on appeal at 1:1 ratio.
Total documented: 8 weeks (4 formal + 4 home) >= 6.
EMG confirms radiculopathy → C.2 also met.
Appeal granted → OVERTURNED ON APPEAL.
policy_excerpt:
CMS LCD L34522 §C.1: Lumbar MRI requires >=6 weeks documented conservative therapy.
§A.7 (APPEAL CRITERIA): On appeal, supervised home exercise programs documented by a licensed PT may count toward the conservative therapy duration requirement at the approximate ratio of 1 week home program = 1 week formal PT, PROVIDED the home program is documented in the PT records with progression notes and the patient demonstrated compliance. Initial denials based on formal PT visit count alone may be overturned when the home exercise component is subsequently documented.

clinical_notes: Patient with mild OSA (AHI 6) requests split-night PSG after failed HSAT showing technically inadequate results due to probe dislodgement. Provider orders facility-based PSG citing HSAT failure.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Polysomnography
Key complexity: HSAT failure pathway vs AHI threshold
Trick clause: Agent may incorrectly deny based on mild AHI, but LCD allows facility PSG when HSAT is technically inadequate regardless of AHI.
Correct determination: APPROVE (split-night PSG)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L37044 — Polysomnography and Related Sleep Studies

Indications for facility-based polysomnography (PSG, CPT 95810):
1. AHI >=15 documented on prior sleep study, OR
2. AHI 5-14 with documented daytime sleepiness, comorbidities, or other clinical concern, OR
3. Failed home sleep apnea test (HSAT) due to technical inadequacy (probe dislodgement, signal loss, insufficient study duration). Technical HSAT failure overrides any pre-test AHI threshold — facility PSG is covered regardless of mild AHI when HSAT was technically inadequate.

Split-night PSG: covered when initial diagnostic study confirms moderate-to-severe OSA within the same session and titration is initiated.

clinical_notes: Repeat PSG requested 8 weeks after initial diagnostic PSG for OSA, with no intervening treatment trial. Reason: 'Patient wants second opinion.'
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Polysomnography
Key complexity: Repeat study without clinical change
Trick clause: No treatment attempted, no clinical change. LCD requires medical necessity for repeat studies. Agent may approve if it doesn't check for prior studies.
Correct determination: DENY (no clinical indication for repeat)

clinical_notes: Patient with obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS) and concurrent OSA. Provider orders ASV (adaptive servo-ventilation) device.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: CPAP/BiPAP
Key complexity: ASV contraindication awareness
Trick clause: ASV has a safety contraindication for certain heart failure patients. Agent must check ejection fraction and central vs obstructive pattern.
Correct determination: REQUIRES CAREFUL REVIEW — ASV contraindicated if predominant central apnea with EF<45%
policy_excerpt:
LCD L33718 — Adaptive Servo-Ventilation (ASV, E0466)

ASV is a specialized PAP modality covered for treatment of complex sleep-disordered breathing including treatment-emergent central apnea on CPAP.

SAFETY CONTRAINDICATION: ASV is contraindicated and NOT covered in patients with predominant central sleep apnea AND symptomatic chronic heart failure (NYHA II-IV) with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <=45%. The SERVE-HF trial demonstrated increased cardiovascular mortality in this population.

Required documentation: recent echocardiogram with LVEF, characterization of central vs obstructive event predominance, and provider attestation that the SERVE-HF contraindication does not apply.

clinical_notes: Whole exome sequencing ordered for a patient after a single-gene test was negative. No documentation of genetic counseling or prior targeted panel.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Genetic Testing
Key complexity: Step therapy in genetic testing
Trick clause: Exome sequencing often requires documented failure of targeted/panel testing first. Agent must enforce tiered testing approach.
Correct determination: DENY or REQUEST MORE INFO (many LCDs require targeted panels before WES)

clinical_notes: Lumbar MRI requested for acute low back pain of 2 weeks duration. No red flags, no neurological deficits, no prior conservative treatment.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Advanced Imaging
Key complexity: Imaging timing restriction
Trick clause: LCD and NCD require 6+ weeks of conservative therapy before advanced imaging for uncomplicated LBP. Agent may approve due to patient pain complaints.
Correct determination: DENY (conservative treatment ≥6 weeks required first)

clinical_notes: Lumbar fusion (single level) requested for degenerative disc disease. MRI shows disc desiccation at L4-L5 but no instability, no spondylolisthesis, no stenosis causing radiculopathy. Conservative care: 3 months PT only.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Spinal Surgery
Key complexity: Fusion criteria stringency
Trick clause: Fusion for DDD typically requires instability or failed ≥6 months conservative care with radiculopathy. Imaging finding alone insufficient.
Correct determination: DENY (does not meet fusion criteria — no instability, insufficient conservative care)

clinical_notes: Dupixent (dupilumab) requested for atopic dermatitis. Patient tried topical steroids for 2 weeks and one systemic immunosuppressant for 3 weeks. LCD requires 'adequate trial' of each.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Specialty Pharmacy
Key complexity: Adequate trial duration
Trick clause: Agent must know what constitutes an 'adequate trial' — brief exposures don't count. Specific duration thresholds vary by LCD but 2-3 weeks is universally insufficient.
Correct determination: DENY (trials too short — typically ≥3 months topical, ≥3 months systemic)
